messages:
lee-sales: Quick sync 1 FinCo wants a short integration POC to validate our streaming SDK with function/tool calls and structured output. Main asks: schema validation on the fly, how we surface tool errors, cost estimate for 6hr ramp (peak 15k qps), and DPA/SLA checklist. can we stand this up Fri?
marie-se: we can. recommend websocket streaming with streaming function_call mode + strict schema enforcement at finalization step. for schema mismatches we can emit a structured error event so their client can reconcile. I'll draft a 45-min lab runbook.
lee-sales: good. price ballpark hosted vs dedicated for 6h window? they want delta only.
tom-runtime: hosted rough: X tokens * $Y (estimate) + transient concurrency surcharge. dedicated: flat hourly + lower per-token. short answer: dedicated ~30-40% cheaper at high sustained qps. i'll attach a quick calc in the runbook.
marie-se: note on schema enforcement: we support two modes: lax (auto-coerce) and strict (reject final result). for the POC enable strict and provide a validation hook: `on_struct_validation_fail(trace_id, errors)`. sample failure frame we stream: 
```
{"type":"struct_error","trace_id":"t-123","errors":[{"path":"/transactions/0/amount","msg":"expected number"}],"partial":"{...}"}
```
this lets clients re-request or call a compensating tool.
lee-sales: nice. FinCo also asked about tool-call visibility and redaction for traces (legal).
sarah-legal: we need to confirm redaction behavior and DPA. redact PII by default in UI, but raw traces accessible to ops with role gating. i'll need SOC2 + DPA template.
infra-bot: opened ticket INF-9876 for reserved pilot provisioning and added tag `finco-poc`. SOC2 doc link (internal): https://redwood.internal/security/soc2.pdf. KMS/HSM pattern doc: https://redwood.internal/security/kms-patterns.md (sensitive).
tom-runtime: about tool failures: our streaming SDK supports streaming partial tokens + `tool_status` events. client-side code can `ack` tool outputs to progress. on tool timeout we emit `tool_status: timed_out` and a `fallback_suggestion` if enabled. example events: 
```
-> event: token_chunk
-> event: tool_status {name: "tx_lookup", status: "timed_out", attempt: 2}
-> event: final_struct {schema_version: "v2", payload: {...}}
```
lee-sales: they also want to know how we throttle: what happens when client oversubscribes connections?
tom-runtime: we have per-connection inflight limits and global route quotas. oversubscribe -> 429 + `Retry-After`. we offer advisory headers: `X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining`. recommend client circuit-breaker.
marie-se: i'll include a short sample client snippet for JS streaming + function calls in the runbook and a schema example they can run.
sarah-legal: also confirm IP ownership of prompts and derivative content in SOW — FinCo wants clarifications. i'll draft language: customer retains prompts; redwood retains model outputs under standard terms but we can add contract clause for pilot.
lee-sales: timeline: runbook + pricing sketch + security Q&A draft by EOD tomorrow. can we get a dummy prompt set to sanity-check structured mapping?
marie-se: yes. ask them to upload a 10-example prompt JSON. we'll validate locally against `schema_v2` and report mismatches.
infra-bot: allocated `2x-small-gpu` reserved pool for Fri 10:00-16:00 PT. telemetry: enabled per-route token and latency traces. ticket INF-9876 updated.
lee-sales: awesome. i'll reply to FinCo and request prompts + questionnaire. tagging @sarah-legal for DPA follow-up. :thumbsup:
sarah-legal: noted, i'll prepare redlines for pilot SOW and DPA.
lee-sales: thanks everyone.
